A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same layer-wise usable information (LI) approach. All 10 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2 support comparison, including figures, equations, references, and v2's Appendix A. v1 has no appendix; much of its background material is relocated to Appendix A in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original experiments on CoQA, QuAC, and CondaQA, including answerability detection, model comparisons, prompt analyses, and layer ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical evaluations and adds prompt tests, SQuAD/NQ detection results, and QuAC calibration experiments.

M1.justification: The underlying LI computation remains a sum of context-versus-null entropy differences across layers of a pretrained model. Section 4.6 adds an optional fitted logistic-regression mapping from LI scores to probabilities for calibration evaluation. The revised pseudocode and LM-head explanation clarify the base computation without establishing a different underlying detector.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates contextual QA on CoQA, QuAC, and CondaQA with no, open-ended, and binary prompts. v2 adds SQuAD and NQ evaluations described as fact-based hallucination detection (Table 4), plus forced-answer, irrelevant, misleading, self-reflective, and explicit-certainty prompt scenarios on QuAC (Tables 2–3). These substantially broaden the evaluated conditions.

E2.justification: The main AUROC baseline suite is retained. v2 adds final-layer VI to the prompt-error comparison, reports Slobodkin et al. first- and last-layer probes in Table 4, and evaluates verbalized-confidence comparators following Tian et al. in Tables 6–7. Slobodkin et al. was previously discussed without this reported comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100-example prompt analyses, classification accuracy for SQuAD/NQ, and QuAC ECE evaluation after logistic calibration on 10 or 100 held-out training examples. The original AUROC metric, stated development-set evaluation, balanced answerability ratio, and model sizes remain. These additions substantially expand evaluation design; the SQuAD/NQ sampling and implementation details remain sparse.

E4.justification: v2 adds score-distribution analysis, prompt relevance and certainty tests, computational-cost estimates, and calibration analyses. The prompt-error analysis changes from CoQA to QuAC and adds a final-layer VI comparison. Conversely, v1's explicit sixth-layer/all-but-last-layer comparison and correctness-stratified ROC analysis (Figures 6–7) disappear. The cumulative-layer analysis is retained in revised form.

E5.justification: Both versions show error bars in their prompt-analysis figures without defining their statistical meaning. Neither specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's 100-example averages and calibration training-set sizes describe samples and evaluation settings, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence: Table 4 reports LI accuracy of 74.78/76.42% on SQuAD and 55.93/57.26% on NQ without/with binary prompts, alongside new prompt, cost, and ECE results. Retained results also change: plotted Llama3 8B CoQA LI AUROC is approximately 79 in v1 Figure 3b versus 65 in v2 Figure 6b, without an explained setting revision. Table 1 changes the open-ended Asta response from incorrect to correct while retaining its VI/LI values. Earlier ROC and partial-layer result entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's claimed LI non-negativity, independence, and monotonicity properties, its optimal-distribution/negligible-approximation assumptions, and the formal DPI subsection. Equation 3 corrects the reversed entropy difference within v1 Equation 5, consistently using null-context entropy minus contextual entropy. These materially revise the formal specification and asserted properties. Most foundational VI definitions are relocated to Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain training-free LI for unanswerability detection, sensitivity to prompt ambiguity, and the advantage of aggregating information across layers. The reordered emphasis and explicit 'test-time' wording preserve these meanings. New experiments primarily support existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning prompt relevance, mechanically forced answers, robustness to misleading instructions, justified abstention, computational efficiency, and calibration. It removes the earlier explanation attributing Llama's performance to greater caution. The Limitations paragraph remains unchanged. Some new interpretations overreach: Table 2 does not uniformly place forced answers below binary prompts, and Table 4 contradicts the claim that binary-prompt gains are greatest for LI.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents projection through the pretrained LM head, averaging over question tokens, calibration data separation, and baseline sampling details. Section 4.5 specifies 10 P(TRUE) demonstrations and 50 semantic-entropy samples with 20-shot prompts. These are newly disclosed details; the stated reduction from 20 demonstrations concerns cited prior work, not an established change from v1.

R1.justification: The expanded Related Work section distinguishes contextual from factual hallucinations and positions LI against hidden-state, attention, and intervention approaches, adding works including Chuang, Burns, Azaria, Chen, Li, Simhi, and Zhang. Benchmark and calibration references also expand. The earlier discussion of Hewitt's conditional probing and several DPI-related citations are removed, substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 moves Related Work before the method, relocates most background to Appendix A, rewrites the method explanation and pseudocode, and places prompt ambiguity before unanswerability in the experiments. Existing experimental interpretations are extensively rewritten. The title ordering, author list, and acknowledgments also change. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond merely inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening correlation plot with distributions, redraws layer plots, adds a computation flowchart, expands the prompt-analysis display, and reorganizes dataset/model comparisons. Table 1 is redesigned around prompt types with shortened context and no difficulty column. Six additional tables present new evidence, while earlier correlation and ROC displays are removed. These are extensive changes to visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the LI sign inconsistency, clarifies computation, and adds useful prompt and calibration tests. However, it removes direct partial-layer and ROC checks, changes retained Llama3 results without explanation, and introduces interpretations contradicted by its tables, including Table 4's claimed largest prompt gains for LI. The PDFs do not establish whether the revised scores correct earlier errors or reflect different conditions. These unresolved reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment despite clearer exposition and broader evidence.
